Scattermap cluster objects

Source: R/zz-gen-scattermap.R
go_scattermap_cluster.Rd

The object for the cluster of a scattermap trace (go_scattermap()). go_scattermap_cluster() creates one, with exactly its properties; a named list with the same properties works too.

Usage

go_scattermap_cluster(
  arg = NULL,
  ...,
  color = NULL,
  enabled = NULL,
  maxzoom = NULL,
  opacity = NULL,
  size = NULL,
  step = NULL,
  skip_invalid = FALSE
)

Arguments

arg

Optional named list, or graph object of the same type, to initialise properties from. Named arguments take precedence.

...

Not used: properties must be named in full.

color

Sets the color for each cluster step. Color: a CSS color string or R color name, or a vector of these.

enabled

Determines whether clustering is enabled or disabled. Logical.

maxzoom

Sets the maximum zoom level. At zoom levels equal to or greater than this, points will never be clustered. Number in the interval [0, 24].

opacity

Sets the marker opacity. Number in the interval [0, 1], or a vector of these.

size

Sets the size for each cluster step. Number in the interval [0, Inf], or a vector of these.

step

Sets how many points it takes to create a cluster or advance to the next cluster step. Use this in conjunction with arrays for `size` and / or `color`. If an integer, steps start at multiples of this number. If an array, each step extends from the given value until one less than the next value. Number in the interval [-1, Inf], or a vector of these.

skip_invalid

If TRUE, silently drop invalid properties instead of raising an error.

Value

A go_scattermap_cluster object (a named list).

Details

Nested objects are named lists, or objects of the constructors their arguments name. Every property is checked against the plotly.js schema when the object is created or modified. A property may be a one-sided formula (color = ~col): it is kept, and evaluated in the data (then checked) when its trace is added to a figure with add_<trace>() or add_trace().

Examples

quakes |>
  go_figure() |>
  add_scattermap(
    lat = ~lat,
    lon = ~long,
    cluster = go_scattermap_cluster(color = "red")
  )
